findings.issue: The initial client component (team-card-list.tsx) imported PokemonCard, whose runtime import of spriteUrl from the server-only api.ts broke the build (turn 20); the design didn't anticipate the client/server boundary.
findings.suggestion: Before writing a client component, check whether anything in the import chain pulls 'server-only' modules; keep card rendering server-side and push only the interactive button to the client.

findings.issue: Wrote the ad-hoc Playwright probe to /tmp where the repo's node_modules can't resolve, costing one failed run before copying it into the work directory.
findings.suggestion: Run verification scripts from the repo root or import playwright by absolute path on the first try.

findings.issue: Grepped app/node_modules/next for the cookies API before confirming node_modules was installed at all.
findings.suggestion: Check installation state before introspecting dependency types; after npm install, a tsc pass makes the type check redundant anyway.

findings.issue: pkill -f patterns matched its own shell, killing the cleanup command (exit 143).
findings.suggestion: Use kill with stored PIDs only, or exclude the current shell from the pattern.

findings.issue: Relied on training memory for Next 16's async cookies() ('maybe not needed' to check docs) without consulting the bundled skill/docs or web.
findings.suggestion: When a framework API is central to the architecture and the version is newer than your knowledge, spend one call confirming it in the local Next dist types or docs.

summary: A near-exemplar session: requirements and architecture were worked out before any code, all edits applied first time, each of the three failures was diagnosed precisely and fixed at the root, and the work ended with a full-suite pass plus a hand-written browser probe of the exact scenarios the spec warns about. The only waste is a handful of avoidable bash fumbles and one client/server boundary misstep that cost a rewrite of one small file.
